description: Policy for the four survey measurements that are gated. The measurements themselves stay in scripts/survey/, which never fails; these rules decide what counts as a regression. Baselines live in jscpd-ratchet.json, cognitive-complexity-ratchet.json, type-coverage-ratchet.json and ast-grep-ratchet.json.

ast-grep.description: Structural reliability findings present when the gate was established: requests without deadlines, dropped errors, retries without idempotency, locale-dependent comparisons. Keyed by rule, file and enclosing symbol rather than line, with an occurrence index so a second finding in the same symbol is a new entry rather than a free one. Entries may only disappear.
ast-grep.rationale: The other three survey ratchets bound taste; this one bounds defects. Every rule here describes something that passes review, passes types, passes lint, and then fails against a real network, a real clock, or a Turkish locale. It was the only defect-class measurement in the repository that could grow without failing anything.

jscpd.description: Copy-paste clone pairs present when the gate was established, keyed by the file pair rather than by line numbers so editing inside a clone does not churn the baseline. Entries may only disappear.

cognitive-complexity.description: Functions exceeding each cognitive-complexity band when the gate was established. A function emits one entry per band it crosses, so improving a score removes entries and worsening one adds them. Entries may only disappear.
cognitive-complexity.rationale: 15 is the first band because that is where sonarjs's own default sits and where a function stops fitting in one screen of attention. The higher bands exist so a function that is already over 15 cannot quietly triple: crossing 25, 50 or 100 is a new finding even though the function was already on the list.

type-coverage.rationale: Tolerance is much tighter than the coverage ratchet's 0.5 points because this measurement is over hundreds of thousands of expressions and barely moves; a 0.5 point allowance would hide thousands of new `any`s. The absolute floor is well beneath every current project and exists to catch a project that collapses rather than to rank the ones above it.
